content: @María Inés de Frutos Fernández Can you (or some other people knowldegable about valuations in Mathlib) have a quick look at this? It is just adding two instances, but I'd like to make sure there is no problem with these before maintainer merging.

Only just looking now, but the PR adds one instance and it's a Prop and these can essentially never cause problems.

I guess that in general the only bad thing which could ever plausibly happen is that typeclass inference needs to solve IsCyclic (ValueGroupWithZero K)ˣ for some K which isn't a local field, and then takes a long time failing to find IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K, but given that if you go to docs#IsNonarchimedeanLocalField and then click on Instances in the docs, you get none at all, this means that any search for [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] will just try the local context and then immediately give up.

Kevin Buzzard said:

the PR adds one instance and it's a Prop and these can essentially never cause problems.

This is very much not true. The instance could create a costly loop

Oh interesting! Are you saying "Prop instances in general" or "this particular instance"? Do you agree with my analysis that this particular instance is safe because there are no instances of IsNonarchimedeanLocalField in mathlib?
Prop instances in general. This instance looks completely fine since its key is specific enough
(ie it is not a forgetful inheritance instance)
